title: RESIDUAL OF CA-535's remediation: the new argument-hint quoting-rationale comment states a YAML rule that two siblings in the same 14-skill family contradict, and the rule is not correct as written. Three of the 14 plugins/edm/skills/*/SKILL.md argument-hint values contain a literal | -- orchestrator:7 (quoted, with the comment), test:7 (unquoted) and metrics:7 (unquoted) -- so the asserted rule is followed at 1 of 3 sites and the comment added to make the exception read as an exception instead makes two conforming siblings read as bugs. The claim is also wrong: | is a YAML block-scalar indicator only in the FIRST character position of a value, and all three values begin with <, which is not an indicator character, so all three are ordinary plain scalars and orchestrator's quoting is optional rather than required. Live proof in the same directory: test:7 and metrics:7 have shipped unquoted through eleven audit rounds and through validate:manifest's frontmatter parse. Contrast the genuinely-forced case at plugins/git/skills/commit/SKILL.md:5, where the constraint is the ': ' in 'optional type override: feat|fix|...', not the pipes. Matters because this is shipped prompt-surface text in a plugin whose thesis is that a documented convention is a contract, and because the false claim originated in round 10's own L7-003 write-up, propagated into ledger entry CA-535, and was copied verbatim into the file from there -- CA-535 is closed, so nothing will revisit it. FIX: preferably drop the quotes at orchestrator:7 so all three |-containing siblings agree (12 of 14 sites are already unquoted), keeping a comment that names the real constraint (quote only when the value starts with a YAML indicator character or contains ': '); alternatively keep the quotes, correct the comment, and quote test:7 and metrics:7 to match. Amend CA-535's ledger entry either way. Optionally pin: assert the set of argument-hint values containing | is uniform in quoting, positive control = one perturbed value.

bin/edm-state:5341 is the plugin's last RETURN-scoped cleanup trap with no signal arms, diverging from the sibling CA-481(a) hardened this round, and CA-481(c)'s new sweep is structurally blind to it. Two functions mktemp a scratch file into a function-local and clean up via a RETURN trap: evals/tiering-matrix.sh:158-161 now uses 'RETURN EXIT' plus three signal arms with the rationale at :148-157 naming the exact failure mode ('RETURN-only leaked $tmp on a die (exit 2, no RETURN) or a SIGINT mid-self-test'), while edm-state:5341 is still a bare trap 'rm -f "$_pxt_ignfile"' RETURN. pattern_extract_titles (:5326-5394) creates the file at :5340 then runs an awk pass at :5349/:5360/:5382 -- the longest-lived statement between creation and removal, the same window CA-449 and CA-481(b) were each filed on -- so a signal there leaks ${TMPDIR}/edm-pxt-ignored.XXXXXX. Both call sites run the function in a subshell (:5541 process substitution, :5654 command substitution), so an EXIT arm is correctly scoped and the sibling's fix applies directly. THE CONSISTENCY CONCERN IS THE PIN, NOT THE LEAK: CA-481(c)'s sweep at wave7-smoke.sh:9636-9682 cannot see this site in either arm -- the 'combined' arm only flags EXIT paired with a real signal in one statement and a bare RETURN trap pairs nothing, and the 'no-hup' arm is FILE-granular (:9656-9661, keyed on FILENAME) while edm-state installs HUP traps at :695/:1510/:6081, so the file is green regardless. The sweep was landed because the convention was 'stated in prose in one file and enforced nowhere', and the one remaining non-conforming site is the one its chosen granularity exempts -- the same all-but-one loop shape as CA-496, CA-231, CA-270 and CA-531. Blast radius is honestly small (update-patterns is a low-frequency operator command; one small file in TMPDIR), hence P2 on consistency and durability grounds rather than impact. FIX: mirror the sibling -- trap 'rm -f "${_pxt_ignfile:-}"' RETURN EXIT plus the three signal arms, with the ${_pxt_ignfile:-} guard for the reason tiering-matrix.sh:150-153 documents (process-wide trap can fire again at EXIT after 'local' has left scope, and a bare expansion would trip set -u); then add a third sweep arm asserting every trap line naming RETURN also names EXIT, one predicate in _ca481_sweep with a scratch positive control in the :9686-9698 shape.

CA-496 CONFIRMED STILL OPEN, UNCHANGED -- DO NOT MINT A NEW ID, reconcile against existing CA-496. The CLI-family durability loop at wave7-smoke.sh:6733 (was :6328 in round 10; the line moved, the content did not) still enumerates nine helpers and omits edm-lint-staged-artifacts, the tenth PATH-exposed helper, created by CA-436's own remediation, and the delegate for the plugin's most privileged hook. The comment at :6757-6759 still reads 'so all 12 print_help call sites in the plugin are covered, not just the 9 bin/ helpers'; the true counts are 13 and 10. No live defect -- bin/edm-lint-staged-artifacts:47 sources the shared library and :50 uses the ${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0} caller convention -- the finding is that the one property this loop exists to provide, durability, is exactly what the newest and most privileged member lacks. The asymmetry that hides it is unchanged: lint:bash-syntax derives its file set from the tree, so the negative CA-005 ban at :6729-6732 covers the new file automatically while the positive assertions at :6733-6747 do not. Fourth consecutive round surviving, and now the only member of the round-10 L7 assignment still open in a round that closed the two other undercount-by-one loop findings (CA-502, CA-531). FIX: add edm-lint-staged-artifacts to :6733 and correct :6758's counts to 13/10; better, derive the list from the bin/edm-* glob minus the underscore-prefixed libraries so the loop is self-extending and the class retires.

N1 -- bin/edm-lint-staged-artifacts' exit-code contract is inverted relative to the bin/ family (:8-10: exit 2 = violation, exit 1 = setup error; the family uses 1 = violation, 2 = setup/usage). Documented in its own EDM-HELP header and in plugins/edm/CLAUDE.md's hooks-behaviour table, and dictated by the host's PreToolUse contract where only exit 2 blocks. False-alarm filter 1 (documented and technically justified). Unchanged; carried from rounds 9-10.

N2 -- bin/edm-lint-staged-artifacts mixes diagnostic prefixes: script-name-prefixed on the CLI-facing argument-handling path (:49-50), [EDM]-prefixed elsewhere on the hook-facing path. Two internally-uniform layers with different audiences, consistent with round 8's disposition L7-N06. False-alarm filter 3 (intentional for operational reasons).

N3 -- POSIX [ ] tests throughout bin/edm-lint-staged-artifacts where the sibling bin/ scripts use [[ ]]. Residue of the sh hook string this file was extracted from (CA-436); harmless under its #!/usr/bin/env bash shebang at :1. False-alarm filter 2/3.

N4 -- the bare 'help' token is accepted at bin/edm-lint-staged-artifacts:50 (-h|--help|help) and by edm-init and evals/score-artifacts.sh, but not by edm-check-skill-sync, edm-compare-eval or evals/tiering-matrix.sh. Standing as CA-289 with an explicit do-not-re-file disposition ('Two lenses saw it, neither claimed it'). Nothing changed this round; recorded so the synthesizer can reconcile against CA-289 rather than mint a new ID.

N6 -- .gitlab-ci.yml:293 and :632 both carry an EXIT-only trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT where the plugin convention is the four-signal split. Container-ephemeral, already dispositioned as round 8's L5-N6, and deliberately outside the bin/ + bin/tests/ + evals/ scope that both CA-481's convention statement and CA-481(c)'s sweep (wave7-smoke.sh:9668-9672) take -- these are job-script fragments inside YAML, not shell source files. Recorded only so a future round knows the count went from one (round 10) to two by design and does not treat :632 as a new regression. False-alarm filter 3.

N7 -- the twelve-agent frontmatter family is now fully pinned and fully consistent, no finding. CA-529 (fixed this round) normalized the last diverging field: all twelve agents/edm-audit-*.md now carry the byte-identical line 'tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, Write', asserted at wave7-smoke.sh:1750-1756 with a positive control at :1758-1768, and the fix took the recommended direction (dropping the inert KillShell/BashOutput grants from the eleven rather than adding them to the synthesizer). model: opus / effort: max / maxTurns: 30 / color: cyan / disallowedTools: Edit, NotebookEdit were already uniform. N8 -- CA-130 reproduced for an 11th consecutive round. The JSONL schema was therefore taken from the launch prompt's restated fallback, exactly as D22/CA-130 prescribes, and both the report and this JSONL were returned as chat text for the orchestrator to write.
